newsitem.title: UK: Whitbread half year profits up 14 percent.
newsitem.headline: Whitbread half year profits up 14 percent.

text.p: Whitbread Plc said Tuesday that its profits rose by 14 percent in the first half of the year and Chairman Sir Michael Angus said he expected recent levels of growth to continue in its beverage, food and hotel markets.

The brewer, which also operates hotels and restaurants, said its profits in the first six months of the year grew to 177.5 million pounds ($290 million) as Britain experienced a growth in visitors from overseas.
The company said its hotel business doubled profits and sales in the six months ended Aug. 31, with occupancy levels and room rates much higher.

"The number of foreign tourists to Britain is growing very, very fast. They spent 13 to 14 billion pounds ($21.2 billion to $22.9 billion) last year and half of that in London," Chief Executive Peter Jarvis said in a statement.

Americans flocked to Whitbread's 16 Marriott hotels during the period as a result of a marketing link-up with Marriott in the United States, adding 5 percentage points to occupancy levels at some Marriott hotels.
Whitbread acquired 16 Marriott hotels in Britain for some 185 million pounds ($302 million) last August.
The company also owns a chain of about 130 low budget Travel Inns, which Jarvis said will be expanded at the rate of about one every 10 days to reach 300 by the end of the year 2000.
Jarvis also said British consumers were feeling better, spending much more on leisure and the upward trend was set to continue for at least two years.
He said consumers spent more eating out during the half year with Pizza Hut, jointly owned with Pepsico, and T.G.I. Friday's sales ahead by about 20 percent.
The company's restaurant and leisure division saw pretax profits rise 58 percent to 56.3 million ($91.9 million).
Whitbread's beer company increased profits by 12 percent to 30.8 million pounds ($50.3 million) on sales that were 8 percent ahead, pushed higher by the acquisition of the Labatt and Wadworth brands.
